item.title: Filters as a localization of nets
item.description: arXiv:2611.28921v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Based on different notions of subnet in the literature, we define categories of nets and investigate their categorical relationships. We show that the category of proper filters with filter-preserving functions is, up to equivalence, a localization of four of these categories.
item.dc:creator: Germ\'an I. Gomero Ferrer, Renan M. Mezabarba

item.title: Admissible balanced pairs over cleft extensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.29392v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(B, A, i, e, l)$ be a cleft extension of abelian categories such that $e$ has a right adjoint $r$. It is proved that $(C, D)$ is an admissible balanced pair in $B$ if and only if $(\operatorname{add}(lC), \operatorname{add}(rD))$ is an admissible balanced pair in $A$. When the extension is directed with respect to a finite product decomposition of $B$, the lifting of complete hereditary cotorsion pairs $(C, Y)$ and $(X, D)$ to $A$ is characterized by the vanishing of first derived functors. Under a compatibility condition, the pair of special classes $(\Delta(C), \nabla(D))$ is then shown to be admissible balanced if and only if $(C, D)$ is. As an application, for rings $A, B$ and a $(B, A)$-bimodule $U$ of finite flat dimension over $A$ and finite projective dimension over $B$, the triangular matrix ring $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A & 0\\ U & B\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is left virtually Gorenstein if and only if $A$ and $B$ are.
item.dc:creator: Junpeng Ren, Zheng-Gang Wu, Mengzhen Zhu

item.title: Decomposition of completeness and the universality of the Daniell extension
item.description: arXiv:2611.29433v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An integration system is a triple $(X,L,I)$: a set $X$, a Riesz subspace $L$ of $\mathbb{R}^X$, and a continuous positive linear functional $I$ on $L$. We introduce the category Int whose morphisms are pullbacks along maps of the base spaces. The main result is that the Daniell extension defines a functor from Int to DInt and is left adjoint to the inclusion of the full subcategory DInt of Daniell closed systems, those with $L^1=L$, usually called complete. So DInt is reflective and the Daniell extension is its reflector. The content lies in a decomposition: a system is Daniell closed if and only if it satisfies the monotone convergence theorem and is closed under modification on null sets, and neither can be dropped. The second corresponds to completeness of the measure. The decomposition is a real-valued phenomenon: for extended-real-valued functions the second condition follows from the first. Daniell closedness of the codomain cannot be omitted. The inclusion of the category of systems satisfying the monotone convergence theorem also has a left adjoint, but its reflector is not the Daniell extension. Under the Stone condition that second reflection consists of the integrable functions measurable for the $\sigma$-algebra generated by $L$. For an arbitrary system, $L^1$ splits as the sum of that part and the functions supported on null sets, so the gap between the two reflections is exactly the completion of the measure. Finally, if morphisms are replaced by positive linear maps between Riesz spaces, they see only the quotient of $L$ by the null functions, where the Daniell extension gives the Banach completion. So the distinction between an abstract completion and a concrete realization survives as categorical structure only where morphisms are maps of base spaces. In sum: the Daniell counterpart of the completion of a measure space, in categorical language.
item.dc:creator: Hayato Saito

item.title: Homotopical interpretation of directed Van Kampen
item.description: arXiv:2611.30197v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct the Grandis model structure on directed spaces with $\Delta$-generated underlying spaces and on the full subcategory of $\Delta$-Hausdorff objects. In either setting the model structure is left proper, and its weak equivalences are precisely the maps that induce equivalences of fundamental categories in the sense of Grandis. The fundamental category functor preserves all small homotopy colimits with values in the folk model structure on small categories. For a union of two induced directed subspaces, the union square is a homotopy pushout precisely when Grandis's categorical pushout formula holds. His covering theorem gives this conclusion whenever the interiors of the two subspaces cover the space.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Gaucher

item.title: Alain Badiou's Mistake: Two Postulates of Dialectical Materialism
item.description: arXiv:1301.1203v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Originally published in 2013, this revised article constitutes the first stage of a two-part intervention that revisits Alain Badiou's deployment of topos theory in Being and Event and Logics of Worlds. It interrogates the structural and philosophical consequences of taking the category-theoretic foundations of mathematics seriously, extending the formal boundaries of mathematical discourse. This part focuses on Logics of Worlds, which emerged as Badiou's response to his own theory of subjectivity. While revisiting structures implicit in his reading of Cohen's proof of the independence of the continuum hypothesis, I demonstrate how his concept of 'dialectical materialism' remains constrained by set-theoretic ontology and localic topos theory - essentially a theory of intuitionistic logic. In particular, Badiou's claim that categorical thinking does not substantially change mathematics overlooks the true geometric momentum driving topos theory. While the primary contents of this article are technical, I further explore how Badiou's formal omissions critically impact his philosophical project. This is especially visible in regard to his 'postulate of materialism' - a device he utilizes to promote dialectical materialism as a credible alternative to science. Through its category-theoretic reframing, I show that the postulate actually encapsulates two structurally different conditions, one of which directly constrains his own project while the other part captures a type of atomism juxtaposed with Badiou's condescending assessment of democracy. By leveraging such claims indebted to his pre-committed, logicist comprehension of mathematics, Badiou reinstitutes an absolutist Truth-doctrine and an ultimately despotic political program against a genuine concept of multiplicity. His errors thus hardly constitute merely an inadvertent formal slip, but indicate a deeper, political intent.
item.dc:creator: Antti Veilahti

item.title: A note on split extension classifiers of perfect objects
item.description: arXiv:2208.01133v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is well known that the automorphism group of a perfect group has trivial center. This is a consequence of the fact that for a perfect group the centralizer of the normal subgroup of inner automorphisms of its automorphism group is trivial. We find a categorical explanation for this fact by showing that for a semi-abelian category $\mathbb{C}$ satisfying (WNH), if $X$ is a perfect object in $\mathbb{C}$ such that the split extension classifier $[X]$ exists, then the centralizer of the \emph{conjugation} morphism $c_X : X\to [X]$ is trivial and hence the center of $[X]$ is trivial. Our proof depends on the following fact, which we show holds in an arbitrary semi-abelian category satisfying (WNH). If $f:X\to Y$ is a central extension and $\theta_1$, $\theta_2$ and $\phi$ are internal object actions of $B$ on $X$, $X$ and $Y$, respectively, such that $f:(X,\theta_i)\to (Y,\phi)$ is an internal $B$-action morphism, then $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ restrict to the same action on $[X,X]$. Using this latter fact we also prove that (UCE) is a consequence of (WNH) alone (rather than of (WNH) together with (SH) as previously known).
item.dc:creator: James R. A. Gray

item.title: Gene ologs: a categorical framework for Gene Ontology
item.description: arXiv:1909.11210v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Gene Ontology (GO) is the most widely used resource for the functional annotation of genes and gene products. It unifies biological knowledge across species through a dynamic, controlled vocabulary, and it is now primarily represented in the Web Ontology Language (OWL), a logic-based language that supports automated reasoning. Ologs (ontology logs), introduced by Spivak and Kent, offer a different language for knowledge representation, grounded in category theory: concepts are types, functional relationships are aspects, and declared equalities between paths are facts. Ologs come with features that are not part of the standard use of GO: path equations, universal constructions (products, coproducts, pullbacks and pushouts), a database reading in which instance data are set-valued functors, and functors with which ontologies can be compared and merged. In this work we take an initial step towards Gene ologs, i.e. ologs for GO. We fix conventions for reading GO terms as olog types, examine which GO relations can be represented as aspects and which must instead be represented as spans, illustrate each olog construction with GO examples, show that standard GO annotations and GO Causal Activity Models (GO-CAM) can be represented as olog instance data subject to checkable constraints, and describe how functors and pushouts can be used to compare and merge Gene ologs. We also discuss what ologs do not provide relative to OWL. We regard Gene ologs as complementary to, rather than a replacement for, the OWL representation of GO.
item.dc:creator: Yanying Wu

item.title: The Balmer spectrum of integral permutation modules
item.description: arXiv:2507.05892v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the Balmer spectrum of the small derived category of permutation modules of a finite group over a commutative Noetherian ring. In this generality, we obtain a set-theoretic description of the spectrum. Under certain mild additional assumptions on the base ring, we describe its topology by reducing the problem first to the modular locus and then to the case of elementary abelian groups. Furthermore, we introduce a twisted cohomology ring in this context, which allows us to realize the spectrum, in the case of elementary abelian $p$-groups, as a Dirac scheme. This extends recent work of Balmer and Gallauer from the setting of ground fields to the more general setting of commutative Noetherian rings.
item.dc:creator: Umesh V Dubey, Juan Omar G\'omez

item.title: Auslander correspondence for higher stable dg categories and cluster Morita theory
item.description: arXiv:2608.30740v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a cluster Morita theorem: every pretriangulated dg category with a $d$-cluster tilting subcategory is realized as the $d$-cluster dg category of that subcategory regarded as a connective dg category. Reversing the Amiot--Guo construction, this yields a bijection between $d$-stable dg categories and pretriangulated dg categories with a chosen $d$-cluster tilting subcategory. Our Auslander correspondence characterizes $d$-stability by coherence, weak global dimension at most $d+1$, and a $(d+1)$-shifted duality on finitely presented modules. For a locally finite $d$-stable dg algebra over a field, right $(d+1)$-Calabi--Yau structures on its perfectly valued derived dg category correspond bijectively to right $d$-Calabi--Yau structures on its $d$-cluster dg category. In characteristic zero, this removes the pseudo-compact enhancement hypothesis from Keller--Liu's theorem on Amiot's conjecture. Via Koszul duality, we characterize $d$-stability over any field for locally finite minimal completed dg path algebras (and their analogues for graded species) by explicit conditions on the graded arrows and the quadratic differential. For $d=1$, these are deformed derived mesh algebras of Dynkin type; for $d=2$, they are complete twisted Ginzburg dg algebras, yielding via cluster Morita theory a twisted analogue of Amiot's conjecture in arbitrary characteristic without a Calabi--Yau hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Ryu Tomonaga
